jurisdiction_body: New York State Public Service Commission / Department of Public Service
rule_citation: NYS Standardized Interconnection Requirements (SIR), effective 2026-02-09, filed in compliance with the order in Case 24-E-0621 issued 2026-01-23; PSL 66-j (solar/farm waste/fuel cell/micro-CHP/micro-hydro net metering) and PSL 66-l (wind); VDER Value Stack orders in Case 15-E-0751
applies_to: IOU only - the six PSC-regulated electric corporations (Con Edison, Orange & Rockland, Niagara Mohawk/National Grid, NYSEG, RG&E, Central Hudson). A single statewide SIR governs all six; they do not have separate interconnection procedures, only utility-specific technical requirements documents referenced by the SIR. LIPA/PSEG Long Island (state authority), municipal electric utilities and rural co-ops are NOT PSC-jurisdictional and set their own rules - see the second NY row.
nem_status: Full retail NEM (Phase One NEM) reported still open to mass market, running alongside the VDER Value Stack (net billing / value-of-DER)
nem_successor: VDER Value Stack (Phase One VDER Order, Case 15-E-0751, issued 2017-03-09) is the successor for non-mass-market projects; mass-market residential and small commercial may elect Phase One NEM (volumetric 1:1 netting) with a 20-year term and no annual cash-out per the Order Establishing Net Metering Successor (Case 15-E-0751, issued 2020-07-16). A monthly Customer Benefit Contribution (CBC), $/kW-DC, applies to mass-market and small-commercial BTM generation interconnected on or after 2022-01-01. 2026 utility-published CBC rates, res/small-comm: net-metered PV $0.97-$1.83 per kW-month; Value Stack PV $0.49-$1.28 per kW-month.
nem_cap_res_kw: 25 (PSL 66-j(1)(d) residential solar, kW AC; 100 kW for a farm operation on a residential meter; 25 kW residential wind under PSL 66-l; 25 kW residential micro-hydro; 10 kW micro-CHP and residential fuel cell)
nem_cap_nonres_kw: 2000 (PSL 66-j(1)(d) non-residential solar, kW AC; also 2000 kW non-residential fuel cell, micro-hydro and farm waste; 2000 kW non-residential wind under PSL 66-l). The SIR itself covers DG and/or ESS up to 5000 kW AC.
nem_aggregate_cap: PSL 66-j(3)(a) sets a first-come-first-served statutory cap of 1% of the utility's 2005 electric demand; PSL 66-j(3)(b) authorises the PSC to raise it, and the PSC raised it to 3% (2012) and 6% (2014). Reported (secondary) that in 2015 the PSC let the aggregate cap float pending the NEM successor, so it is not a live constraint - not verified against the order text.
export_credit_basis: 1:1 retail volumetric netting under Phase One NEM (mass market); value-of-DER stack under VDER Value Stack - monetary crediting of net hourly injections built from LBMP energy value, capacity/ICAP value, environmental E-Value, Demand Reduction Value and Locational System Relief Value
export_credit_value: No single statewide rate. Value Stack credit is $/kWh, varies by utility, NYISO load zone, hour and vintage; Phase One NEM credits at the customer's full retail volumetric rate.
credit_rollover: Monthly rollover of excess credits (PSL 66-j(3)(e)-(h) for remote-crediting configurations); Value Stack credits carry over as monetary bill credits
annual_true_up: Phase One NEM reported to have no annual cash-out (2020 Net Metering Successor Order); PSL 66-j(4)(c) annual payment at utility avoided cost applies to legacy/grandfathered net metering. Annual-cash-out removal is secondary-sourced.
ic_standard: IEEE 1547-2018 / UL 1741 Supplement B. SIR Sec II.H requires NRTL certification to the most recent revision of UL 1741 including Supplement B (UL 1741 SB), with settings specified in each utility's technical requirements document.
ic_fast_track_kw: 300 (SIR Sec I.B Exception 1: inverter-based systems above 50 kW up to 300 kW certified to UL 1741 SB may use the 6-step expedited process at utility approval; utilities are encouraged but not required to use it)
ic_simplified_kw: 50 (SIR Sec I.B: 6-step expedited process for systems 50 kW or less; utility has 10 business days to determine completeness/eligibility/approval)
ic_application_fee: No application fee for systems 50 kW or less (SIR Sec I.B Step 3). Above 50 kW an application fee applies but its dollar amount is set in SIR Appendix F, which was not retrievable - NOT VERIFIED. Other fixed SIR fees: $750 non-refundable Pre-Application Report fee (credited to the application fee if the application is filed within 15 business days); $2,500 Supplemental Screening Analysis fee with actual costs billable up to $5,000; Energy Storage System Protection and Control Review fee = $500 + $4/kW capped at $3,000.
ic_study_trigger_kw: No fixed kW study trigger. Systems above 50 kW up to 5 MW enter the 11-step process: the utility runs a Preliminary Screening Analysis (screens A-F, 15 business days). Passing all screens with no Interconnection Facilities or Distribution Upgrades means no study. Failing a screen lets the applicant choose a results meeting, a Supplemental Screening Analysis (screens G-I) or a full Coordinated Electric System Interconnection Review (CESIR). CESIR is therefore triggered by screen failure or applicant election, not by size alone. Systems 50 kW or less in underground secondary network areas may also require a CESIR (SIR Sec I.C Exception 1).
external_disconnect: Required for systems larger than 25 kW and for non-inverter-based systems 25 kW or less - external, manual, visible, gang-operated, load-break, lockable in the open position, customer-owned (SIR Sec II.D). Waived for inverter-based systems 25 kW or less.
insurance_required: No statewide requirement. PSL 66-j(5)(b)(i) and 66-j(5-a)(c) bar an electric corporation from requiring additional liability insurance from a net-metered customer-generator whose equipment meets the established safety standards. The SIR imposes no insurance requirement.
ic_timeline_days: Per-step business-day deadlines, not one statutory clock: 10 BD application completeness/eligibility/approval determination; 15 BD Preliminary Screening Analysis; 20 BD Supplemental Screening Analysis; 20 BD ESS Protection and Control Review; 10 BD verification testing after notice; 5 BD final acceptance letter. CESIR duration is project-specific and not fixed by the SIR.
grid_charging_allowed: Yes - the SIR expressly studies an ESS's Maximum Import as well as Maximum Export (Sec I.E Step 2 and Glossary), so grid charging is a declared, permitted operating characteristic. On the compensation side, the Joint Utilities' Value Stack Hybrid Facilities tariff Options C and D allow the storage to be charged from both the paired generator and the utility system and allow both to inject for compensation, while Options A and B restrict charging to the paired generator so that injections keep E-Value, ICAP and Market Transition Credit eligibility. The precise crediting of grid-charged kWh under Options C/D was not verified against tariff text, and the Joint Utilities have petitioned to apply standby and buyback service to Option C/D hybrids whose NEM-eligible generator is smaller than the paired ESS (Case 15-E-0751) - disposition of that petition not verified.
non_export_option: Yes - Appendix K requires the applicant to declare the ESS's Maximum Export (which may be set to zero or a limited value) and the utility studies the facility at those declared operating characteristics; for ESS requiring a CESIR the utility supplies testing procedures that use the applicant's load management control systems to limit reverse power (SIR Sec I.E Step 2). Systems neither designed to operate nor operating in parallel with the utility system are outside the SIR entirely (SIR Sec I.A). A change of operating characteristics later requires a new Appendix K and a contract amendment.
storage_counts_toward_cap: Yes for SIR tier routing - which process applies (Sec I.B vs I.C) is set by the sum of the AC nameplate ratings of all DG and ESS behind the point of common coupling, and maximum export is capped at 5 MW AC (SIR Sec I.A and I.E Step 1). Whether ESS kW counts against the PSL 66-j net metering system-size caps is not addressed in the SIR - Unclear.
standby_charge: Authorized, with a net-metering carve-out. PSL 66-j(4)(d) bars an electric corporation from imposing back-up, standby or demand charges on a net-metered customer-generator, except that ordinary demand charges may be applied on the same terms as to non-generating customers in the same class. Utility standby-service and buyback tariffs apply outside net metering (e.g. Con Edison General Rule 20 standby service, Rider Q standby pilot rate, SC-11 buyback).
standby_threshold_kw: Set by each utility's tariff, not statewide.

jurisdiction_body: Long Island Power Authority (Board of Trustees); PSEG Long Island administers as LIPA's agent
rule_citation: LIPA Tariff for Electric Service, Small Generator Interconnection Procedures (SGIP) addendum; separate LIPA Smart Grid Small Generator Interconnection Procedures (SGSGIP) track
applies_to: LIPA / PSEG Long Island only. LIPA is a state authority and is NOT subject to the PSC's Standardized Interconnection Requirements, PSL 66-j or PSL 66-l; it runs its own SGIP.
nem_status: Full retail NEM (Phase One Net Billing, 1:1 monthly volumetric crediting) for Mass Market residential/small-commercial customers and pre-2018/2020 Large Onsite projects, running alongside a Value Stack (VDER-analogue) tariff for Large Onsite/Offsite projects and Community Distributed Generation (CDG). Verified against LIPA Tariff for Electric Service Leaf Nos. 34A-34K (Sec I.C.15, Net Metering Generators) and LIPA Statement No. 102 (Value Stack Credits/VSC), effective 2026-09-01.
nem_successor: Value Stack (VSC) tariff, a VDER-style compensation construct - confirmed in LIPA Tariff Leaf 34C Sec I.C.15.c)(5)-(6) and priced in LIPA Statement No. 102 (VSC), effective 2026-09-01. Applies to Large Onsite/Offsite projects and CDG; Mass Market/Phase One NEM customers are not forced onto it and may keep 1:1 net billing (and may pair on-site storage without losing NEM eligibility).
nem_cap_res_kw: 25 kW AC for Residential Solar, Wind, Micro-Hydroelectric, or hybrid combinations; Residential Farm 100 kW (Solar) or 500 kW (Wind) or 500 kW (hybrid); Farm Waste 5,000 kW; Micro-CHP 1-10 kW; Fuel Cell <=10 kW. [LIPA Tariff Leaf 34A/34A-1, Sec I.C.15.a)] - LIPA voluntarily mirrors the PSL 66-j/66-l residential thresholds even though it states it is not subject to PSL 66-j.
nem_cap_nonres_kw: 5,000 kW AC for Nonresidential Solar, Wind, Farm Waste, Fuel Cell or Micro-Hydroelectric. [LIPA Tariff Leaf 34B, Sec I.C.15.b)(1)] - notably larger than the PSC utilities' 2,000 kW PSL 66-j cap; existing 2,000-5,000 kW generators not yet on Value Stack may opt in to VDER (Leaf 34B, (2)).
nem_aggregate_cap: No statewide-style aggregate/program MW or % cap found in the LIPA Tariff's General Terms and Conditions, unlike the PSC utilities' former 1%->6%-of-2005-peak-load cap under PSL 66-j. Consistent with LIPA's own confirmation that it is 'not subject to PSL Section 66-j' (LIPA Dec-2025 Tariff Changes filing, Exhibit B-3 background section, citing Case 19-E-0079). Current subscription level, if tracked, was not found in this pass.
nem_sizing_rule: Residential (Solar/Wind/Micro-Hydro/hybrid): system capacity <=110% of the customer's prior 12-month consumption or a customer-provided load letter, and within the kW caps above. [LIPA Tariff Leaf 34A, Sec I.C.15.a)(1)] Nonresidential: no consumption-matching sizing rule found beyond the 5,000 kW capacity cap [Leaf 34B].
export_credit_basis: 1:1 retail volumetric netting for Mass Market/Net Billing customers (net excess kWh credited at the same per-kWh rate as non-generating customers in the same rate class, Leaf 34F Sec I.C.15.h)(1)-(2)); value-of-DER stack (Value Stack/VSC) for Large Onsite/Offsite and CDG projects, structurally parallel to the PSC's VDER Value Stack.
export_credit_value: Net Billing: full volumetric retail rate of the customer's own rate class (no separate statewide cents/kWh figure). Value Stack (VSC) components per LIPA Statement No. 102, effective 2026-09-01: Energy Component = NYISO day-ahead zonal LBMP average; Capacity Component Alt.1 (Sept 2026) $0.0339/kWh at 34.3% proxy capacity factor, Alt.2 $0.1797/kWh, Alt.3 $11.0578/kW-month; Environmental Component $0.03103/kWh; Demand Reduction Value $0.4451/kWh (contracted hours); Locational System Relief Value $7.3450/kWh per event; Community Credit $0.0500/kWh (Fuel Cell technology adjustment factor 16%).
credit_rollover: Monthly rollover of banked credits within the service year (banked separately by rating period - peak/off-peak/intermediate - for TOU rate codes; re-mapped when a customer switches rate structure), but not indefinite - see annual_true_up for the yearly cash-out. [LIPA Tariff Leaf 34E-34F, Sec I.C.15.h)]
annual_true_up: At the end of the first year of service and on every anniversary thereafter, LIPA pays the Customer-generator for any remaining banked net-excess-generation credit, valued at the avoided energy price per LIPA's Statement of Market Energy Prices. [LIPA Tariff Leaf 34F, Sec I.C.15.h)(h)] This is an annual cash-out - a real deviation from the PSC row's Phase One NEM, which is reported (secondary-sourced there) to have no annual cash-out.
ic_standard: IEEE 1547 / UL 1741 Supplement B (UL 1741 SB) - the SGIP requires NRTL certification to 'the most recent revision of UL 1741 including Supplement B' with settings per PSEG Long Island's Technical Requirements and Screening Criteria document. [LIPA/PSEG Long Island SGIP, July 2026 ed., Secs I.B and II.B]
ic_fast_track_kw: 300 - SGIP Sec I.B Exception 1: inverter-based systems above 50 kW up to 300 kW, UL 1741 SB certified, may use the expedited process at PSEG Long Island's determination. Mirrors the PSC SIR's 300 kW tier.
ic_simplified_kw: 50 - SGIP Sec I.B: Expedited/Fast Track Process applies to systems 50 kW or less. Mirrors the PSC SIR's 50 kW tier.
ic_application_fee: SGIP application fee $750 for systems 50 kW to 5 MW and $750 for systems 5 MW to 10 MW, payable to PSEG Long Island (PSEG Long Island SGIP Application Instructions). Fee for systems under 50 kW not verified.
ic_study_trigger_kw: No fixed kW study trigger. Systems that fail the Preliminary Screening Analysis (Appendix G technical screens) or whose applicant elects further review proceed to a Supplemental Screening Analysis or a full Coordinated Electric System Interconnection Review (CESIR) - structurally parallel to the PSC SIR's process. [SGIP, July 2026 ed., Secs I.B-I.C]
external_disconnect: Unclear beyond an automatic device. SGIP Sec II.B requires an automatic disconnect device (protective-relay based, sized to code, with over/under voltage and frequency trip functions) that isolates the generator on islanding or LIPA-system-fault detection. The SGIP text located does not separately spell out an external, manual, visible, lockable, gang-operated disconnect switch requirement the way the PSC SIR does for systems above 25 kW; LIPA's Red Book electrical specifications (not reviewed in this pass) may impose one - not verified either way.
insurance_required: No blanket insurance mandate found in the SGIP itself. However, LIPA Tariff Leaf 34C, Sec I.C.15.c)(4) reserves the Authority's right to require a Customer-generator to purchase additional liability insurance (along with added safety/performance standards or tests) when total generating capacity on the same local feeder exceeds 20% of that feeder's rated capacity - a real, feeder-loading-triggered insurance exposure that the PSC row does not have (PSL 66-j(5)(b)(i)/(5-a)(c) bars the PSC utilities from requiring it).
ic_timeline_days: Per-step business-day deadlines, not one statutory clock (mirrors the PSC SIR's structure): 10 BD application completeness/eligibility determination; 15 BD Preliminary Screening Analysis; 10 BD applicant election after screening results; 20 BD Supplemental Screening Analysis; 15 BD contract issuance after passing screens; 10 BD verification testing after installation notice; 5 BD final acceptance letter. CESIR duration is project-specific and not fixed by the SGIP. [SGIP, July 2026 ed.]
storage_allowed: Yes - SGIP Sec I.E and Appendix J define a dedicated Energy Storage System (ESS)/Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) application track covering Hybrid Projects (DG + ESS) and stand-alone storage, within the SGIP's 10 MW aggregate nameplate ceiling.
grid_charging_allowed: Unclear - LIPA SGIP and tariff not verified on grid charging
non_export_option: Yes, structurally: ESS applicants must declare 'Maximum Export' and 'Maximum Import' as operating characteristics in Appendix J, and PSEG Long Island studies the facility at those declared values (which may be set to zero or a limited value), so a limited/non-export configuration is supported. The SGIP text reviewed does not label this a distinct, separately-branded fast-track 'non-export' pathway the way the PSC SIR's Appendix K is described - Unclear if it confers the same study-skipping benefit.
storage_counts_toward_cap: Unclear. LIPA's net-metering size limits (Tariff Leaf 34A/34B) are written against the 'rated capacity' of the Solar/Wind/Farm Waste/Fuel Cell/Micro-Hydroelectric generating equipment, i.e., the generator - neither the Tariff nor the SGIP text reviewed states whether a paired ESS's AC kW is added to that figure for cap purposes. The Tariff does confirm (Leaf 34C, Sec I.C.15.c)(5)) that Mass Market NEM customers may pair storage with an eligible generator and remain on Phase One NEM, so storage does not disqualify a system from net metering - but whether it counts toward the kW ceiling itself was not found.
standby_charge: Service Classification No. 12 - Standby Service (renamed from 'Back-Up and Supplemental Service,' new Rate Code 682 commercial / 179 residential-optional), effective 2026-01-01, replacing the old SC-12 Back-Up and Supplemental Service tariff. Mandatory for on-site self-generating customers who maintain a grid connection, subject to technology (solar/wind) and size-based exemptions; optional for other self-generating customers ('Optional Rate Customers,' requires an AMI meter). Rate = Service Charge + Contract Demand Charge, set on an Allocated-Cost-of-Service, revenue-neutral basis; ~72 existing mandatory commercial customers are phased in from 2026-2030 (full rates from 2031) unless they elect full rates immediately. Service Classification No. 11 - Buyback Service (for customers exporting to the grid) was updated in the same filing to add a Customer Charge and Buyback Contract Demand Charge set equal to the corresponding Standby rates; stand-alone ESS that reach Step 3 of the SGIP process before 2030-12-31 are exempt from the Buyback Contract Demand Charge for 15 years from their in-service date. [LIPA Board materials, 'December 2025 Tariff Changes,' Item 3 - New Rates for Standby Service and Updates to Buyback Service, approved effective 2026-01-01]
standby_threshold_kw: No single kW threshold. SC-12 Standby Service is mandatory for on-site generating customers maintaining a grid connection, with exemptions including generation under 5 kVA and generation under 15% of the customer's maximum potential demand; SC-11 Buyback Service is required for customers who inject power to the grid, subject to similar technology/size exemptions. [LIPA Board materials, 'December 2025 Tariff Changes,' background section]
